title: The Office - Interview Skills 7 - Describing Ones Weaknesses
audio: mp3/253. The Office - Interview Skills 7 - Describing Ones Weaknesses.mp3

segments.en: Hello, everyone, and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Catherine, and today we've got one more episode in our series about interview skills.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们的系列中还有一集关于采访技巧。

segments.en: This is an elementary level series, and we're here today to talk about things that you might not be very good at.
segments.zh: 这是一个基本级别的系列，我们今天在这里讨论您可能不太擅长的事情。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Today we're going to talk about weaknesses, and that is our word for vocabulary preview.
segments.zh: 今天我们将讨论弱点，这是我们词汇预览的词汇。

segments.en: So let's take a look at it now.
segments.zh: 所以让我们现在来看看它。

segments.en: Vocabulary preview.
segments.zh: 词汇预习。

segments.en: Okay, so what is a weakness?
segments.zh: 好吧，那么什么是弱点？

segments.en: A weakness is a thing or an activity or something that you're just not very good at or something that you think you can improve.
segments.zh: 弱点是你只是不太擅长的事物或活动或事物，或者你认为可以改进的东西。

segments.en: Okay, so obviously no one is perfect, and like we saw in the previous lesson, we had a lot of good things about ourselves, key strengths, and now we're going to talk about our weaknesses.
segments.zh: 好吧，显然没有人是完美的，就像我们在上一课中看到的那样，我们有很多关于自己的好东西，关键优势，现在我们要谈谈我们的弱点。

segments.en: Maybe you're a little bit lazy.
segments.zh: 也许你有点懒。

segments.en: That might be a weakness.
segments.zh: 这可能是一个弱点。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: A weakness is the opposite of strength, and that is the topic today, so let's take a listen to today's dialogue.
segments.zh: 弱点是力量的反面，这就是今天的话题，所以让我们来听听今天的对话。

segments.en: Okay, Rebecca.
segments.zh: 好的，丽贝卡。

segments.en: Well I think you've given me a clear impression of your positive qualities, but let's talk a little bit about your weaknesses.
segments.zh: 好吧，我认为您让我对您的积极品质有了清晰的印象，但让我们谈谈您的弱点。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Well it's always more difficult to describe them, isn't it?
segments.zh: 好吧，描述它们总是更困难，不是吗？

segments.en: Definitely, but if you had to pinpoint one weakness, what would it be?
segments.zh: 当然，但如果你必须确定一个弱点，那会是什么？

segments.en: Well as I mentioned before, I do tend to get frustrated if I don't see progress in my work or career.
segments.zh: 正如我之前提到的，如果我没有看到我的工作或职业进展，我确实会感到沮丧。

segments.en: I suppose I'm quite a restless character.
segments.zh: 我想自己是那种不太安于现状的人。

segments.en: My father always taught me to be a high achiever, so...
segments.zh: 父亲一直教导我要努力取得出色的成绩，所以……

segments.en: So would you say if things don't go your way at work, it could easily get you down?
segments.zh: 也就是说，如果工作中遇到不顺心的事，你就容易感到沮丧？

segments.en: Well in a way, yes, but I must say that even if I'm not completely happy in my work, I always give 110%.
segments.zh: 在某种程度上，是的，但我必须说，即使我对工作不完全满意，我总是付出 110%。

segments.en: I would never shirk my responsibilities.
segments.zh: 我永远不会逃避我的责任。

segments.en: I suppose sometimes I expect too much too soon.
segments.zh: 我想自己有时太急于求成，期望过高了。

segments.en: Well you know journalism is a highly competitive world, so you do need to keep pushing yourself, it's true.
segments.zh: 好吧，您知道新闻业是一个竞争激烈的世界，所以您确实需要不断推动自己，这是真的。

segments.en: Okay, well let's move on to talk about the job position here, shall we?
segments.zh: 好吧，让我们继续谈谈这里的工作职位，好吗？

segments.en: Yes, please.
segments.zh: 好的，请。

segments.en: Alright, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So obviously, Rebecca did a very good job at talking about her weaknesses in a very positive way.
segments.zh: 很明显，丽贝卡在以非常积极的方式谈论她的弱点方面做得非常好。

segments.en: So before we get into analyzing that, why don't we take a look at a couple of words she used on Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 所以在我们开始分析之前，我们为什么不看看她在语言外卖上使用的几个词。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: One of the first words that Mr. Parsons used was a clear impression, so impression.
segments.zh: 帕森斯先生使用的第一句话是清晰的印象，所以印象。

segments.en: Alright so I think this is a very common word when people talk about first impressions or I get the impression.
segments.zh: 好吧，当人们谈论第一印象或我得到印象时，我认为这是一个非常常见的词。

segments.en: So what is an impression?
segments.zh: 那么什么是印象呢？

segments.en: Well an impression is like an idea or a feeling.
segments.zh: 印象就像一个想法或感觉。

segments.en: So I can have an impression about something, it means that I don't necessarily understand it really well or I don't have experience with it, but it's an idea that I have about something.
segments.zh: 所以我可以对某事有一个印象，这意味着我不一定很好地理解它，或者我没有经验，但这是我对某事的想法。

segments.en: That's right, so for example, maybe you meet somebody new and you say I get the impression that he is a liar.
segments.zh: 没错，例如，也许你遇到了一个新人，你说我觉得他是个骗子。

segments.en: But maybe then you get to know him and he's not.
segments.zh: 但也许你会认识他，而他不是。

segments.en: So this is your idea about something or the way you feel about something.
segments.zh: 所以这是你对某事的想法或你对某事的感觉。

segments.en: So in this case, Mr. Parsons has a clear impression of her positive qualities.
segments.zh: 所以在这种情况下，帕森斯先生对她的积极品质有着清晰的印象。

segments.en: That means that he has an idea or an understanding of the things that Rebecca is good at, but he wants to know more about her weaknesses.
segments.zh: 这意味着他对丽贝卡擅长的事情有一个想法或理解，但他想更多地了解她的弱点。

segments.en: That's right and Mr. Parsons asked her to try and pinpoint one of her weaknesses.
segments.zh: 没错，帕森斯先生让她尝试找出她的弱点之一。

segments.en: So this word to pinpoint.
segments.zh: 所以这个词要精确定位。

segments.en: This is a great word, I'm not really sure where it comes from in English, but I think it's very visual, you can see what the word means.
segments.zh: 这是一个很好的词，我不太确定它来自英语的位置，但我认为它非常直观，你可以看到这个词的含义。

segments.en: Pinpoint means to locate or identify or really be specific about something.
segments.zh: Pinpoint 意味着定位或识别或真正具体化某事。

segments.en: That's right, so maybe if you go to the doctor and you say that your back hurts, the doctor might ask you to try and pinpoint where on your back you have the pain.
segments.zh: 没错，所以也许如果你去看医生，你说你的背部疼痛，医生可能会要求你尝试确定你背部的哪个部位疼痛。

segments.en: That's right, so it's a way to be specific or very exact about something.
segments.zh: 没错，所以这是一种具体或非常准确的方式。

segments.en: Okay, so if she had to pinpoint something, she said, well, I do get a little bit frustrated.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以如果她必须确定一些东西，她说，好吧，我确实有点沮丧。

segments.en: Okay, so frustrated is a way you feel.
segments.zh: 好吧，很沮丧是你的感受。

segments.en: I feel frustrated, he is frustrated.
segments.zh: 我感到沮丧，他很沮丧。

segments.en: It's basically a feeling that you get when you have to do something, but you don't think you can do it or maybe something annoys you and you get frustrated.
segments.zh: 当你必须做某事时，这基本上是一种你的感觉，但你认为你做不到，或者可能会惹恼你，你会感到沮丧。

segments.en: For example, when people tap like this and I'm working, I get frustrated because it's a distraction.
segments.zh: 例如，当人们像这样点击并且我正在工作时，我会感到沮丧，因为这会分散注意力。

segments.en: Okay, so everyone has different things that frustrate them.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以每个人都有不同的事情让他们感到沮丧。

segments.en: Now if we take a look at this word, it is actually an adjective and we usually use it, you get frustrated or as you said, you feel frustrated.
segments.zh: 现在，如果我们看一下这个词，它实际上是一个形容词，我们通常使用它，你会感到沮丧，或者正如你所说，你会感到沮丧。

segments.en: So remember, it may look like a verb, but it's actually an adjective that ends in ed, frustrated, to get frustrated.
segments.zh: 所以请记住，它可能看起来像一个动词，但它实际上是一个形容词，以 ed 结尾，沮丧，沮丧。

segments.en: He got frustrated or we feel very frustrated.
segments.zh: 他感到沮丧，或者我们感到非常沮丧。

segments.en: Okay, and well, apart from being frustrated, she also said that she is a restless character.
segments.zh: 好吧，好吧，除了沮丧之外，她还说她是一个不安分的角色。

segments.en: Okay, so someone is restless if they don't like to stay in one place all the time.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以如果他们不喜欢一直呆在一个地方，他们就会焦躁不安。

segments.en: That means someone who wants to move around or to go places or to travel or to see new things is restless.
segments.zh: 这意味着想要四处走动或去地方、旅行或看到新事物的人是不安的。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So she has a restless character, that means she likes to move around.
segments.zh: 所以她有一个不安的性格，这意味着她喜欢四处走动。

segments.en: She doesn't like to stand still in one place.
segments.zh: 她不喜欢站在一处静止不动。

segments.en: Maybe she gets bored very easily.
segments.zh: 也许她很容易感到无聊。

segments.en: Okay, so that's somebody that would be restless.
segments.zh: 好吧，那是一个会不安的人。

segments.en: But moving on, she also said that she doesn't like to shirk her responsibilities.
segments.zh: 但继续前进，她也说她不喜欢推卸责任。

segments.en: Okay, you often hear these words go together.
segments.zh: 好吧，你经常听到这些话一起去。

segments.en: So responsibilities are things that we need to do, right?
segments.zh: 所以责任是我们需要做的事情，对吧？

segments.en: Things that other people expect us to do, to shirk a responsibility means to not do something that you're supposed to do.
segments.zh: 其他人希望我们做的事情，推卸责任意味着不做你应该做的事情。

segments.en: It means to avoid responsibility or to push it away.
segments.zh: 这意味着避免责任或推开它。

segments.en: Okay, so it's a verb, to shirk your responsibilities.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以这是一个动词，推卸你的责任。

segments.en: You shouldn't shirk your responsibilities.
segments.zh: 你不应该推卸责任。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Alright, so a lot of interesting key words there.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以那里有很多有趣的关键词。

segments.en: Why don't we listen to the dialogue again and we'll be back with Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 我们为什么不再听一次对话，我们会带着 Fluency Builder 回来。

segments.en: Okay Rebecca, well I think you've given me a clear impression of your positive qualities, but let's talk a little bit about your weaknesses.
segments.zh: 好吧，丽贝卡，好吧，我认为你让我对你的积极品质有了清晰的印象，但让我们谈谈你的弱点。

segments.en: Okay, well it's always more difficult to describe them, isn't it?
segments.zh: 好吧，描述它们总是更难，不是吗？

segments.en: Definitely, but if you had to pinpoint one weakness, what would it be?
segments.zh: 当然，但如果你必须确定一个弱点，那会是什么？

segments.en: Well as I mentioned before, I do tend to get frustrated if I don't see progress in my work or career.
segments.zh: 正如我之前提到的，如果我没有看到我的工作或职业进展，我确实会感到沮丧。

segments.en: I suppose I'm quite a restless character.
segments.zh: 我想自己是那种不太安于现状的人。

segments.en: My father always taught me to be a high achiever, so...
segments.zh: 父亲一直教导我要努力取得出色的成绩，所以……

segments.en: So would you say if things don't go your way at work, it could easily get you down?
segments.zh: 也就是说，如果工作中遇到不顺心的事，你就容易感到沮丧？

segments.en: Well, in a way, yes.
segments.zh: 好吧，在某种程度上，是的。

segments.en: But I must say that even if I'm not completely happy in my work, I always give 110%.
segments.zh: 但我必须说，即使我对工作不完全满意，我也总是付出 110%。

segments.en: I would never shirk my responsibilities.
segments.zh: 我永远不会逃避我的责任。

segments.en: I suppose sometimes I expect too much too soon.
segments.zh: 我想自己有时太急于求成，期望过高了。

segments.en: Well, you know journalism is a highly competitive world, so you do need to keep pushing yourself, it's true.
segments.zh: 好吧，你知道新闻业是一个竞争激烈的世界，所以你确实需要不断推动自己，这是真的。

segments.en: Okay, well let's move on to talk about the job position here, shall we?
segments.zh: 好吧，让我们继续谈谈这里的工作职位，好吗？

segments.en: Yes please.
segments.zh: 是的，请。

segments.en: So we've picked out three key phrases for you on Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 因此，我们在 Flueny Builder 上为您挑选了三个关键短语。

segments.en: Let's take a look at those now.
segments.zh: 现在让我们来看看这些。

segments.en: Starting with Mr. Parson saying, so would you say if things don't go your way at work, it could easily get you down?
segments.zh: 从帕森先生说，你会说如果事情不按你的方式工作，它很容易让你失望吗？

segments.en: Two great phrases there.
segments.zh: 那里有两个很棒的短语。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So the first phrase, if things don't go your way.
segments.zh: 所以第一个短语，如果事情没有按照你的方式进行。

segments.en: So this is kind of a funny phrase when you think about it because they go your way like to me or what is my way.
segments.zh: 所以当你想到它时，这是一个有趣的短语，因为它们像我一样对我或我的方式是什么。

segments.en: This basically means if things do not happen in a way that makes you happy or in a way that you expect.
segments.zh: 这基本上意味着如果事情没有以让你快乐的方式发生，或者以你期望的方式发生。

segments.en: Okay, so we could say he lost his job, he couldn't pay his bills, things just didn't go his way.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以我们可以说他失去了工作，他付不起账单，事情并没有按照他的方式进行。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So things are not happening as he planned or as he expected.
segments.zh: 所以事情没有像他计划或他预期的那样发生。

segments.en: You can also say the opposite.
segments.zh: 你也可以说相反。

segments.en: So he won the lottery and he also met a really beautiful girl who wanted to be his girlfriend.
segments.zh: 所以他中了彩票，他还遇到了一个非常漂亮的女孩，她想成为他的女朋友。

segments.en: Things were going his way.
segments.zh: 事情正在按他的方式进行。

segments.en: Okay, very good.
segments.zh: 好，很好。

segments.en: So if things are going your way, it's good.
segments.zh: 所以如果事情顺利进行，那就很好了。

segments.en: If things aren't going your way, then it's bad.
segments.zh: 如果事情没有按照你的方式进行，那就很糟糕了。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Okay, and so if things aren't going Rebecca's way, does that mean that it could easily get her down?
segments.zh: 好的，所以如果事情没有顺利进行，这是否意味着它很容易让她失望？

segments.en: Okay, so to get you down or to get someone down means to make you sad, upset or frustrated like that where we just heard.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以让你失望或让某人失望意味着让你悲伤、沮丧或沮丧，就像我们刚刚听到的那样。

segments.en: So you could ask someone like, Marco, what gets you down?
segments.zh: 所以你可以问像马可这样的人，是什么让你失望了？

segments.en: Rainy days.
segments.zh: 雨天。

segments.en: That's a good one.
segments.zh: 说得好。

segments.en: Yeah, rainy days get me down too.
segments.zh: 是的，下雨天也让我失望。

segments.en: So it's kind of a way of saying what makes you sad or depressed or what makes you unhappy.
segments.zh: 所以这是一种说是什么让你悲伤或沮丧或是什么让你不开心的方式。

segments.en: Or in this case, if something doesn't happen as you planned it, if it doesn't go your way, does that make you sad?
segments.zh: 或者在这种情况下，如果没有按照您的计划发生某些事情，如果它没有按您的方式进行，那会让您难过吗？

segments.en: Does that get you down?
segments.zh: 这会让你失望吗？

segments.en: Okay, very good.
segments.zh: 好，很好。

segments.en: So a very good question there.
segments.zh: 所以一个很好的问题。

segments.en: And she responded that kind of, yeah, that does happen, but she always tries to give 110%.
segments.zh: 她回应了那种，是的，这确实发生了，但她总是试图付出 110%。

segments.en: Okay, so this is a really funny phrase because you think I can give everything I have.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以这是一个非常有趣的短语，因为你认为我可以付出我所拥有的一切。

segments.en: I can work really hard and that's 100%.
segments.zh: 我可以非常努力地工作，那是 100%。

segments.en: But we say 110% means you do more than you can.
segments.zh: 但我们说 110% 意味着你做的比你能做的更多。

segments.en: It's like pushing yourself more than is possible.
segments.zh: 这就像强迫自己而不是可能。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So this is a very common phrase in sports and business.
segments.zh: 所以这是体育和商业中非常常见的短语。

segments.en: People are saying, for example, I always remember my coach saying, I want you guys to give me 110% out there.
segments.zh: 例如，人们在说，例如，我总是记得我的教练说，我希望你们给我 110% 的钱。

segments.en: That means I really want you to try very hard to do as much as possible.
segments.zh: 这意味着我真的希望你尽可能地努力做。

segments.en: Even more than your best, more than you think you can do.
segments.zh: 甚至比你最好的还要多，比你想象的还要多。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So again, it refers to the effort that you put into something.
segments.zh: 再说一次，它指的是你付出的努力。

segments.en: It can be in business, sports, anything.
segments.zh: 它可以在商业、体育、任何事情中。

segments.en: And she's basically saying, I always do more than my best.
segments.zh: 她基本上是在说，我总是做的比我最好的还要多。

segments.en: I do as much as humanly possible.
segments.zh: 我尽可能多地做人。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Okay, so a lot of great stuff there from Rebecca.
segments.zh: 好的，丽贝卡有很多很棒的东西。

segments.en: Why don't we listen to her one last time and we'll be back in a bit.
segments.zh: 我们为什么不最后一次听她的，我们会回来一会儿。

segments.en: Okay, Rebecca.
segments.zh: 好的，丽贝卡。

segments.en: Well I think you've given me a clear impression of your positive qualities.
segments.zh: 好吧，我认为你让我对你的积极品质有了清晰的印象。

segments.en: But let's talk a little bit about your weaknesses.
segments.zh: 但是让我们谈谈你的弱点。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Well it's always more difficult to describe them, isn't it?
segments.zh: 好吧，描述它们总是更困难，不是吗？

segments.en: Definitely.
segments.zh: 当然。

segments.en: But if you had to pinpoint one weakness, what would it be?
segments.zh: 但如果你必须确定一种弱点，那会是什么？

segments.en: Well as I mentioned before, I do tend to get frustrated if I don't see progress in my work or career.
segments.zh: 正如我之前提到的，如果我没有看到我的工作或职业进展，我确实会感到沮丧。

segments.en: I suppose I'm quite a restless character.
segments.zh: 我想自己是那种不太安于现状的人。

segments.en: My father always taught me to be a high achiever, so...
segments.zh: 父亲一直教导我要努力取得出色的成绩，所以……

segments.en: So would you say if things don't go your way at work, it could easily get you down?
segments.zh: 也就是说，如果工作中遇到不顺心的事，你就容易感到沮丧？

segments.en: Well in a way, yes.
segments.zh: 在某种程度上，是的。

segments.en: But I must say that even if I'm not completely happy in my work, I always give 110%.
segments.zh: 但我必须说，即使我对工作不完全满意，我也总是付出 110%。

segments.en: I would never shirk my responsibilities.
segments.zh: 我永远不会逃避我的责任。

segments.en: I suppose sometimes I expect too much too soon.
segments.zh: 我想自己有时太急于求成，期望过高了。

segments.en: Well you know journalism is a highly competitive world, so you do need to keep pushing yourself, it's true.
segments.zh: 好吧，您知道新闻业是一个竞争激烈的世界，所以您确实需要不断推动自己，这是真的。

segments.en: Okay, well let's move on to talk about the job position here, shall we?
segments.zh: 好吧，让我们继续谈谈这里的工作职位，好吗？

segments.en: Yes, please.
segments.zh: 好的，请。

segments.en: Alright, so talking about weaknesses, I think one of the common mistakes when people talk about weaknesses is they say they work too much.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以说到弱点，我认为人们谈论弱点时常见的错误之一是他们说他们工作太多了。

segments.en: And everyone says you should never say that in an interview.
segments.zh: 每个人都说你永远不应该在采访中这么说。

segments.en: Yeah, I think it's a bad way to talk about yourself because a boss or an employer really wants to hear a real weakness.
segments.zh: 是的，我认为谈论自己是一种糟糕的方式，因为老板或雇主真的想听到一个真正的弱点。

segments.en: And I work too hard is a way of saying, I have no weaknesses.
segments.zh: 而我工作太努力是一种说法，我没有弱点。

segments.en: I'm actually really, really perfect.
segments.zh: 我真的，真的很完美。

segments.en: I just think it's a lazy answer.
segments.zh: 我只是认为这是一个懒惰的答案。

segments.en: So maybe you should avoid saying I work too hard and really focus on things that you do have to work on.
segments.zh: 所以也许你应该避免说我工作太努力，真正专注于你必须努力的事情。

segments.en: And then I think the key is to say that I know this is something that I have a hard time with, I know this is a weakness and I'm trying to improve it.
segments.zh: 然后我认为关键是说我知道这是我很难接受的事情，我知道这是一个弱点，我正在努力改进它。

segments.en: Yeah, I remember in some of the interviews I've had, I think my common answer was sometimes I'm very late, I'm not very punctual.
segments.zh: 是的，我记得在我接受过的一些采访中，我想我的共同回答是有时我很晚，我不是很准时。

segments.en: But you know, it's a real weakness and it may seem like difficult, but then you give it a little spin by saying, yeah, I'm sometimes not very punctual, but then I try to make up for it, maybe staying more time at the office, or sometimes I try to wake up a little bit earlier and make it on time.
segments.zh: 但你知道，这是一个真正的弱点，可能看起来很困难，但是你会说，是的，我有时不是很准时，但我试着弥补它，也许在办公室呆更多的时间，或者有时我试着早点醒来 并按时完成。

segments.en: I don't know, something like that.
segments.zh: 我不知道，类似的东西。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So the key there is just to show that you know it's a problem and that you're trying to work on it.
segments.zh: 所以关键只是表明你知道这是一个问题并且你正在努力解决它。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So this is actually the hardest part for me of an interview, talking about yourself in a negative way, because obviously you want to get the job.
segments.zh: 所以这实际上是我面试中最难的部分，以消极的方式谈论自己，因为显然你想得到这份工作。

segments.en: So you want to make sure that the employer has a good idea of yourself, but it's hard.
segments.zh: 所以你想确保雇主对自己有一个好的想法，但这很难。

segments.en: I think it's the hardest part for everyone.
segments.zh: 我认为这对每个人来说都是最难的部分。

segments.en: I don't think it's just you.
segments.zh: 我不认为只有你。

segments.en: Yeah, it's hard.
segments.zh: 是的，这很难。

segments.en: So this is an interesting topic.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个有趣的话题。

segments.en: Why don't you practice and come to our website EnglishPod.com and on our comment section, why don't you tell us what your weaknesses are?
segments.zh: 您为什么不练习并访问我们的网站 Englishpod.com 和我们的评论部分，您为什么不告诉我们您的弱点是什么？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: We hope to hear from you.
segments.zh: 我们希望收到您的来信。

segments.en: Of course, you can also share with us your strengths on our lesson about strengths.
segments.zh: 当然，您也可以在我们的优势课程中与我们分享您的优势。

segments.en: But in this one, I recommend everyone practice this because it will come up at some point and it's good to get the practice in.
segments.zh: 但在这一篇中，我建议每个人都练习这个，因为它会在某个时候出现，并且可以进行练习是很好的。

segments.en: So EnglishPod.com, we hope to see you there.
segments.zh: 所以englishpod.com，我们希望在那里见到你。

segments.en: All right, guys.
segments.zh: 好了，各位。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
